h1: Getting liquid yeast to India alive and checking it on arrival
title: Getting Liquid Yeast to India Alive | Craft Beer School
desc: How to get liquid brewing yeast to India in good health, what to check on arrival and how to build it up before you pitch.
teaser: Liquid yeast does not like long journeys or Indian heat. A few checks on arrival tell you whether your pack is ready to pitch.
standfirst: Liquid yeast opens up strains you cannot buy dry, but every day in transit and every degree above fridge temperature costs you live cells. Here is how to order, receive and check it so your brewery pitches healthy yeast.
sections:
Liquid yeast is live cells suspended in a little wort or nutrient solution. Unlike dry yeast, it has not been dried into a dormant state, so it keeps using its own reserves while it waits. Warmth speeds that up. A pack that spends a few days at 35 °C in a courier van can arrive with a fraction of the healthy cells it left the lab with.

The dry versus liquid yeast trade-off in India is mostly about this journey. Dry yeast tolerates it. Liquid yeast needs a plan.

• Buy from an Indian distributor or yeast bank where you can. A shorter, domestic cold chain beats an international courier.
  • Ask how it ships. Insulated box, ice packs or gel packs, plus the expected time in transit.
  • Time it. Order so it does not sit in a depot over a weekend or public holiday. Monday and Tuesday dispatches are safest.
  • Check the import paperwork. Live microbial cultures may need specific documents at customs. The requirements can change. Your importer or distributor should handle this. Do not ask a friend to carry packs in a suitcase without checking.
  • Order earlier than you need it. Plan on building a starter, which adds a day or two.

1. Temperature. Open the box straight away and slip a probe thermometer between the packs. Cold is good. Warm is not fatal, but it tells you to expect lower viability.
  2. Dates. Note the production or best-before date. Older packs carry fewer live cells.
  3. Pack condition. Some swelling can be normal for packs that contain a nutrient pouch. Leaks, mould or a strong sour or rotten smell on opening are not.
  4. Refrigerate at 2 to 4 °C until you are ready to use it.

A brewery should not guess. A microscope, a haemocytometer and methylene blue stain give you a cell count and viability in about twenty minutes. Live cells break down the dye and stay colourless. Dead cells stain blue. Many brewers aim for 90% or better viability before pitching. Below that, they step up with a bigger starter or discard the pack. Our guide to yeast viability and vitality walks through the counting.

If you do not yet have a microscope, a starter is your viability test. A healthy pack should show clear activity, a krausen or a layer of fresh yeast, within roughly a day.

One pack is sized for a homebrew batch, not a brewpub tank. Professional brewers grow it in steps, often around a tenfold increase in volume at each step, with aerated wort at about 1.036 to 1.040 gravity and steady temperature. A small batch might go from a pack to a 2 litre starter. A 1,000 litre fermenter needs several steps or a dedicated propagation plan. Our guide to making a yeast starter covers the method.

Many brewpubs then harvest and repitch the strain for several generations, so one well-handled import can serve months of brewing.

Record every pack in a simple log: strain, supplier, production date, date received, temperature on arrival, viability if measured and how fast the starter took off. After a few orders you will see which suppliers and which shipping routes deliver healthy yeast and which do not. That evidence is useful when you talk to a distributor about a bad delivery. It also tells you how much margin to build into your starter plan.

Keep the log next to your brew sheets so a yeast problem can be traced back to the pack it came from.

Do not panic and do not pitch it straight into a production batch. Make a small starter, check it with a stain if you can and watch how fast it gets going. A slow, weak starter tells you to step up again or reorder. Pitching a tired pack directly into wort is how breweries get long lag times, stressed fermentations and esters or sulphur they did not plan for.

Yeast handling is the part of brewing that most recipe-led brewers skip. It is also the part that decides whether the same recipe tastes the same every time.
faqs: Can liquid yeast survive shipping to India?
Yes, if it travels cold and fast. Buy domestically where possible, ship with ice packs and avoid weekend transit.
How do I know if my liquid yeast is still alive?
Count it with a microscope and methylene blue stain, or make a starter and watch for clear activity within about a day.
What viability is good enough to pitch?
Many brewers aim for about 90% or better. Lower viability means you need more cells, a bigger starter or fresh yeast.
Can I bring liquid yeast back in my luggage?
Check the current rules for importing live cultures first. Requirements can apply. Heat in transit can also ruin the yeast.
